- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–7 days, then underestimates later — adjust for asymmetric bias toward higher values initially.
- After sharp spikes (e.g., 75→85+), model overshoots and fails to correct, suggesting lag in recalibrating downward — apply dampening factor after peak.
- When sentiment is neutral (all 0.00), model lacks directional bias correction — introduce sentiment-triggered adjustment: if sentiment later turns positive, model should trend upward; if negative, trend downward.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized — model holds high values too long after peaks; add decay term to forecast to reflect natural reversion to recent 10–15 day average.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts often misalign with true values in middle-to-late period (days 15–25) — reduce forecast volatility in this window, especially if sentiment remains flat.
- If true outcome shows sudden drop after spike, model fails to anticipate — add “drop zone” heuristic: if prior 3–5 days show sharp rise, reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 3–5 days unless sentiment confirms continuation.
